# Travel Policy (effective February 2026)

This policy replaces the January 2025 Travel Policy. It covers business travel abroad and domestic travel between Acme offices, for employees and for contractors traveling on Acme's behalf. The per diem rates and hotel caps were raised to reflect higher prices in 2025.

## 1. Approval and booking

Every trip abroad needs the approval of the department VP before booking. Trips are booked through TripDesk. Bookings made elsewhere are reimbursed only if they were cheaper than the TripDesk offer at the time of booking.

## 2. Flights

Economy class is the default. On flights longer than 6 hours, all employees may book premium economy. VP-level employees and above may fly business class on flights longer than 8 hours. Book at least 14 days in advance when possible.

context.title: Acme Flow Architecture Overview
context.text:
## 9. Key design decisions

**Asynchronous by default.** The API only accepts work and enqueues it. This keeps the API fast and protects it from slow third-party tools, at the cost of more complex debugging: a "successful" API call does not mean the run succeeded.

**Checkpoint after every step.** This makes runs resumable after crashes and deploys, and lets customers see exactly where a run failed. The cost is write load on the runs database, which is the main reason for the Kestrel project.

**Cells per region instead of a global platform.** Simpler data residency and a smaller blast radius, at the cost of operating two copies of everything.

**One owner per service.** Every service has exactly one owning team, listed in the Service Catalog. Shared ownership has repeatedly led to slow incident response at Acme.

context.title: Postmortem: flow-api outage (August 19, 2026)
context.text:
# Postmortem: flow-api outage on August 19, 2026

- **Date of incident:** August 19, 2026
- **Severity:** SEV1
- **Duration of full unavailability:** 47 minutes (14:06 to 14:53 Israel time)
- **Affected service:** flow-api in both regions; root cause in auth-service
- **Incident commander:** Tomer Shani (core-api-oncall primary)
- **Reviewed in:** Blue Room, August 27, 2026

## Summary

A configuration change to auth-service reduced its database connection pool from 200 to 20 connections per pod. Token validation requests from flow-api queued behind the small pool and timed out, and flow-api returned errors for 92% of requests at the peak. For 47 minutes the public API, the web app and inbound webhooks were effectively unavailable in both regions. The configuration change skipped the canary stage, because configuration-only changes were not canaried at the time.

context.title: Postmortem: flow-api outage (August 19, 2026)
context.text:
## Root cause

The connection pool size of auth-service was changed from 200 to 20 by a typo in a configuration-only change. Configuration changes were deployed through Conveyor without the canary stage, so the change went to 100% of pods in both regions within 2 minutes. A canary at 5% would have shown the latency increase and rolled back automatically.

## Contributing factors

- No validation of configuration values (for example a minimum pool size).
- flow-api's token validation cache (60 seconds) was too short to absorb the problem.
- It took 12 minutes from the identity page to finding the change, because configuration changes were not shown in the auth-service dashboard.

context.title: Postmortem: flow-api outage (August 19, 2026)
context.text:
## Timeline (Israel time)

- 14:03: An identity engineer merges a configuration change to auth-service intended to set a per-pod connection limit of 200; a typo sets it to 20. Conveyor applies it to both regions in under 2 minutes, without a canary.
- 14:06: flow-api 5xx rate rises to 92%. Customer-facing outage begins.
- 14:09: FlowApi5xxRateHigh pages core-api-oncall. Tomer Shani acknowledges at 14:10.
- 14:15: SEV1 declared, Tomer Shani is incident commander. Status page updated at 14:21.
- 14:19: No flow-api deploy in the last hour; the error breakdown shows `upstream=auth` timeouts. identity-oncall paged.
- 14:31: identity-oncall finds the connection pool change in #deploys.
- 14:41: Rollback of the configuration started with `conveyor rollback auth-service`.
- 14:49: auth-service pods restarted with the correct pool size; error rate dropping.
- 14:53: flow-api error rate back to normal. Outage ends.
- 15:20: Webhook backlog fully replayed.

## When you cannot deploy

- Production deploys are blocked during Quiet Hours unless a CAB exception is granted.
- `billing-service` is frozen from the 1st of the month at 00:00 UTC until the invoice run finishes on the 2nd.
- During an active SEV1 or SEV2, only fixes for that incident are deployed.

To request an exception, post in #cab with the change, the reason it cannot wait, the rollback plan, and the name of an on-call engineer who will watch the deploy.

## Configuration changes

Until September 2026, configuration-only changes (feature flags, connection pool sizes, timeouts) were applied through Conveyor without the canary stage, because they were considered low risk. This changed after the August 2026 flow-api outage: all configuration changes now go through the canary stage like code changes. Feature flags managed in the flag service are not affected; they have their own gradual rollout.

context.text:
# New Hire Laptop FAQ

A quick FAQ for new employees, put together by the IT team. The official rules are in the Laptop and Endpoint Policy.

**Which laptop will I get?**
Engineers, data analysts and designers receive a MacBook Pro 14-inch with an Apple M-series chip, 32 GB of memory and 1 TB of storage. All other employees receive a MacBook Air 13-inch with 16 GB of memory and 512 GB of storage.

**When will I get a new laptop?**
Laptops are replaced every 3 years. IT contacts you a month before the refresh date.

**Why is my laptop so locked down?**
Every Acme laptop is enrolled in Jamf (for macOS) or Intune (for Windows). Full-disk encryption, automatic OS updates, the endpoint protection agent, a 5-minute screen lock and the firewall are mandatory. Laptops that are not compliant for more than 7 days lose access to Okta-protected applications.

**Can my kids use the laptop for homework?**
No. Family members may not use the work laptop.

**I'm working from a café. Anything special?**
On public Wi-Fi, connect to the Acme VPN (Tailscale) before accessing internal systems.

**I lost my laptop. What now?**
Report a lost or stolen laptop to IT (it@acme.example) and to Security (security@acme.example) within 1 hour of noticing. IT will lock and wipe it remotely. You will not be blamed for reporting.

## Quotes

- For purchases above $15,000, at least 3 written quotes are required, or a written single-vendor justification approved by the CFO.

context.title: Postmortem: flow-api outage (August 19, 2026)
context.text:
## Impact

- About 1,140 customer organizations made at least one failed API call.
- About 2.3 million API requests failed with 5xx errors or timeouts.
- Inbound webhooks were buffered on flow-api pods and replayed after recovery; no webhook was lost. Scheduled runs were not affected, because flow-scheduler does not depend on flow-api.
- Monthly availability of flow-api for August 2026 was 99.89%, below the 99.95% monthly commitment for Enterprise customers and the 99.9% commitment for Business customers.
- 203 support tickets, including 31 P1 tickets from Enterprise customers.

context.title: Support Priorities and Escalation
context.text:
## Priorities

- **P1, Critical:** production workflows are down or the customer cannot log in, with no workaround.
- **P2, High:** a major feature is broken or severely degraded; a workaround exists but is painful.
- **P3, Normal:** a problem with limited impact, or a question about expected behavior.
- **P4, Low:** feature requests, cosmetic issues, general questions.

The customer chooses an initial priority; the agent may change it, and must explain why in the ticket.

## First response targets

First response time (FRT) is measured from the creation of the ticket to the first reply by a human agent.

| Priority | Enterprise | Business | Team | Starter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 30 minutes (24/7) | 1 hour (24/7) | 4 business hours | community only |
| P2 | 2 hours | 4 business hours | 1 business day | community only |
| P3 | 8 business hours | 1 business day | 2 business days | community only |
| P4 | 2 business days | 3 business days | 5 business days | community only |

A ticket whose first response comes after the target is counted as an SLA breach in the weekly support report.

context.title: Refund Policy
context.text:
# Refund Policy

This policy tells Customer Support agents when a customer can receive a refund, who approves it, and how it is processed. The customer-facing summary is published on the website; this internal version adds approval limits and processing details.

## Monthly plans

- Customers on monthly billing can cancel at any time. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing month.
- There are no refunds for partial months.

## Annual plans

- A customer may cancel an annual plan and receive a full refund within 14 days of the initial purchase.
- After 14 days, annual plans are not refundable. The customer can turn off auto-renewal, or downgrade at the renewal date.
- Seats added during an annual term are charged pro rata and are not refundable.

context.title: On-call Runbook - flow-api
context.text:
## Severity guide for flow-api

- SEV1: API unavailable or 5xx above 25% in any region, or webhooks dropped.
- SEV2: elevated errors (5-25%) or p99 above 2 seconds for more than 15 minutes.
- SEV3: degradation of a single non-critical endpoint.

## Communication

For SEV1 and SEV2, the incident commander asks Customer Support to update the public status page within 15 minutes of declaring the incident, and every 30 minutes afterwards.

## After an incident

Every SEV1 and SEV2 gets a blameless postmortem, written within 5 business days and reviewed in Blue Room. See the August 2026 postmortem for the most recent flow-api SEV1.

## Professional development

- Each employee may spend up to 4,000 NIS per year on courses, conferences and books related to their role, with manager approval before the purchase.

# Business Expenses and Reimbursement Policy

This policy covers everyday business expenses that employees pay out of pocket and claim back. Travel expenses (flights, hotels, per diem) are covered by the Travel Policy. Purchases from vendors that require a purchase order are covered by the Procurement Policy.

## General principles

- Spend company money as if it were your own. Choose reasonable options, not the cheapest or the most expensive.
- Every expense must have a clear business purpose that you can explain in one sentence.
- Claims are submitted in Spendwise, Acme's expense system, within 60 days of the purchase. Claims submitted later are rejected unless the Controller approves an exception.
- A receipt is required for every expense above 50 NIS (or 15 EUR for Berlin employees). Photos of receipts are accepted.

context.title: On-call Runbook - flow-api
context.text:
### RateLimiterDegraded
The rate limiter fails open: if Redis is unavailable, requests are allowed without limits. This keeps customers working but exposes downstream services to bursts. Inform engine-oncall so they can watch consumer lag.

## Useful commands

- Recent errors for one customer: in Datadog logs, `service:flow-api @org_id:<org> status:error`.
- Pods per region: `kubectl -n flow-api get pods -o wide --context prod-il` (or `prod-eu`).
- Disable an abusive API key temporarily: `acmectl apikey suspend <key-id> --reason "<ticket>"` (requires the on-call role; always notify Customer Support in #support-escalations).

## Retention

- Internal and Confidential documents are reviewed by their owners at least once a year; outdated documents are archived, not deleted, unless the retention schedule requires deletion.
- Customer data is deleted within 30 days after the end of the customer's contract, unless the contract states otherwise.
- Application logs that may contain customer data are retained for 30 days; audit logs for 1 year (3 years for Enterprise customers).

## Responsibilities

- Every document owner sets the classification of their documents.
- The Security team, led by the CISO Tamar Golan, owns this policy and reviews it yearly.
- Violations are handled according to the Security Incident Response Policy.

# Procurement Policy (effective April 2026)

This version replaces the January 2025 Procurement Policy. The approval thresholds were raised to reflect the company's growth and to reduce approval delays for routine purchases, and a fourth level was added for very large contracts.

## Scope

Every purchase of goods or services from an external vendor that Acme pays directly. Everyday out-of-pocket expenses are covered by the Business Expenses Policy, and travel by the Travel Policy.

## Approval thresholds

Purchases are approved according to the total contract value for the first year, including VAT:

| Total value (USD) | Approver |
|---|---|
| up to $7,500 | direct manager |
| $7,500 to $40,000 | department VP |
| $40,000 to $150,000 | CFO |
| above $150,000 | CFO and CEO |

Multi-year contracts are approved according to the total value of all years, not the first year only.

context.title: Acme Flow Architecture Overview
context.text:
## 2. High-level picture

Requests reach Acme Flow through two doors:

1. **The web app** (`web-app`), a React single-page application that customers use to build and monitor workflows. It talks only to the public API.
2. **The public API** (`flow-api`), a REST API used by the web app, by customers' own code, and by inbound webhooks from third-party tools.

Behind the API, the main services are:

- **auth-service:** identity, login, OAuth2/OIDC token issuing and validation, SAML single sign-on for Business and Enterprise customers, and API keys. Every request to `flow-api` is authenticated by calling `auth-service` (with a short local cache of validated tokens, 60 seconds).
- **flow-scheduler:** owns time-based triggers (cron-like schedules) and delayed steps. It decides *when* a run should start and publishes a "run requested" message.
- **flow-engine:** the heart of the platform. It consumes "run requested" messages, loads the workflow definition, and executes steps one by one on a pool of workers, persisting the state of each run after every step so that a run can resume after a crash.
- **connectors-hub:** the integration layer with about 240 connectors to third-party tools. It stores customers' connection credentials (encrypted) and executes actions and polling triggers against third-party APIs, with per-connector rate limiting.

## Overage

- Team: $10 per additional 1,000 runs.
- Business: $7 per additional 1,000 runs.
- Starter workspaces stop running workflows when the monthly limit is reached until the next month or an upgrade.

## Features by plan

- Starter: 5 active workflows, community support.
- Team: unlimited workflows, email support, 2FA.
- Business: everything in Team, SAML single sign-on, audit log (1 year), 99.9% uptime SLA, priority support.
- Enterprise: everything in Business, 99.9% uptime SLA with higher credits, dedicated customer success manager, custom contract terms.

context.title: Security Incident Response Policy
context.text:
## Roles

- **Incident Commander (IC):** the on-call security engineer at first; for SEV1 the CISO, Tamar Golan, or her delegate takes over as IC. The IC coordinates, makes decisions, and owns communication.
- **Technical lead:** the engineer driving the investigation and containment.
- **Scribe:** keeps a timeline in the incident document.
- **Communications lead:** for SEV1 and SEV2, someone from Customer Support or Legal handles customer and regulator communication.

For a SEV1, the IC notifies the ERT within 30 minutes of declaring the incident.

context.title: Postmortem: flow-api outage (August 19, 2026)
context.text:
# Postmortem: flow-api outage on August 19, 2026

- **Date of incident:** August 19, 2026
- **Severity:** SEV1
- **Duration of full unavailability:** 47 minutes (14:06 to 14:53 Israel time)
- **Affected service:** flow-api in both regions; root cause in auth-service
- **Incident commander:** Tomer Shani (core-api-oncall primary)
- **Reviewed in:** Blue Room, August 27, 2026

## Summary

A configuration change to auth-service reduced its database connection pool from 200 to 20 connections per pod. Token validation requests from flow-api queued behind the small pool and timed out, and flow-api returned errors for 92% of requests at the peak. For 47 minutes the public API, the web app and inbound webhooks were effectively unavailable in both regions. The configuration change skipped the canary stage, because configuration-only changes were not canaried at the time.

context.title: Postmortem: flow-api outage (August 19, 2026)
context.text:
## Timeline (Israel time)

- 14:03: An identity engineer merges a configuration change to auth-service intended to set a per-pod connection limit of 200; a typo sets it to 20. Conveyor applies it to both regions in under 2 minutes, without a canary.
- 14:06: flow-api 5xx rate rises to 92%. Customer-facing outage begins.
- 14:09: FlowApi5xxRateHigh pages core-api-oncall. Tomer Shani acknowledges at 14:10.
- 14:15: SEV1 declared, Tomer Shani is incident commander. Status page updated at 14:21.
- 14:19: No flow-api deploy in the last hour; the error breakdown shows `upstream=auth` timeouts. identity-oncall paged.
- 14:31: identity-oncall finds the connection pool change in #deploys.
- 14:41: Rollback of the configuration started with `conveyor rollback auth-service`.
- 14:49: auth-service pods restarted with the correct pool size; error rate dropping.
- 14:53: flow-api error rate back to normal. Outage ends.
- 15:20: Webhook backlog fully replayed.

context.title: Postmortem: flow-api outage (August 19, 2026)
context.text:
## Impact

- About 1,140 customer organizations made at least one failed API call.
- About 2.3 million API requests failed with 5xx errors or timeouts.
- Inbound webhooks were buffered on flow-api pods and replayed after recovery; no webhook was lost. Scheduled runs were not affected, because flow-scheduler does not depend on flow-api.
- Monthly availability of flow-api for August 2026 was 99.89%, below the 99.95% monthly commitment for Enterprise customers and the 99.9% commitment for Business customers.
- 203 support tickets, including 31 P1 tickets from Enterprise customers.

context.title: Postmortem: flow-api outage (August 19, 2026)
context.text:
## Root cause

The connection pool size of auth-service was changed from 200 to 20 by a typo in a configuration-only change. Configuration changes were deployed through Conveyor without the canary stage, so the change went to 100% of pods in both regions within 2 minutes. A canary at 5% would have shown the latency increase and rolled back automatically.

## Contributing factors

- No validation of configuration values (for example a minimum pool size).
- flow-api's token validation cache (60 seconds) was too short to absorb the problem.
- It took 12 minutes from the identity page to finding the change, because configuration changes were not shown in the auth-service dashboard.

context.title: Postmortem: flow-api outage (August 19, 2026)
context.text:
## SLA and customer communication

- Customer Support issued SLA credits to eligible Business and Enterprise customers proactively, according to the SLA in force for 2026, without waiting for customers to request them.
- A public summary of this incident was published on the status page on August 21.

## Action items

1. All configuration changes go through the canary stage in Conveyor. Owner: Boaz Nahum (Platform). Done September 1, 2026.
2. Schema validation with minimum and maximum values for auth-service configuration. Owner: Gil Avraham (Identity). Done September 8, 2026.
3. Show configuration changes as events on all service dashboards. Owner: Platform team. Done September 3, 2026.
4. Evaluate a longer token validation cache with revocation events. Owner: Gil Avraham. In progress, due December 2026.
